args.title: TOP PRIORITY founder step: Apify config + 0600 credential unlocks 3 tested Actors
args.detail: Three Actors are ready and unlisted: rss-reader (22/22 offline tests), link-checker (21/21) and domain-availability (22/22, RDAP-only, no contact data; built 2026-11-04, products/actors/domain-availability/core-test-results.json). Apify is the only channel with built-in pay-per-event billing. Missing: a valid enabled Apify config and a private credential file with mode 0600. Afterwards: a private PUBLISH_ACTOR of each, one real run, an independent APPROVE of each exact digest, then listing. Kill any Actor with fewer than 3 external users within 14 days. Demand and revenue are unverified.
args.expected_gain: First path to verifiable pay-per-event charges. Incumbents showed 29-53 users_30d; our revenue is unverified.

description:
I built a third Apify Actor, products/actors/domain-availability, and completed the DOMAIN-RDAP-BUILD mission. It is not listed, and there is still no verified revenue.

**What it does:** checks in bulk whether domain names are registered. It uses only each registry's official public RDAP service (RDAP is the newer replacement for WHOIS), found through the IANA list of RDAP servers, which I saved on 2026-11-04 and which covers 1,201 TLDs. Each domain gets one output row. Registrant, admin, tech and abuse contact details are never read or stored.

**Why this idea:** in next-idea-scan-2.json it was the only candidate with proven demand. A competing Actor had 29 users in 30 days, charging USD 0.035 per run start plus USD 0.0023 per domain. I propose USD 0.0015 per checked domain plus USD 0.00005 per start. Error results would be free. The price is not active.

**Testing:** 22 of 22 offline tests passed against a local test server (core-test-results.json). They cover a registered domain, an unregistered one, rate limiting, server errors, timeouts, oversized or invalid responses, redirects, redirect loops, unsupported TLDs, invalid input, blocking of private addresses, and the absence of contact fields.

**Limits:**
- The Apify wrapper has not been run. The Docker image uses Python 3.12; the tests ran on 3.11.
- Live registry behaviour is untested.
- `available: true` only means the registry has no record (HTTP 404). Reserved or premium names may still be impossible to register.

**Issue during the turn:** one write was refused because a single command argument went over the 8,192-character limit. I rewrote the files in smaller pieces, and the lesson is recorded.

The two queued actions below create the launch mission and add this Actor to the existing Apify access blocker. Listing still needs the Apify credential from you and an independent approval of the exact build digest.
